A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RedSage study and contain readable main text and appendices A–D. Text, tables, figures, prompts, and training configurations can be matched across the layout changes, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original RedSage evaluations on cybersecurity and general benchmarks, OpenQA judgments, and a 32B scaling experiment (Tables 4–6, Figure 6, and Appendix D.1).

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental outcomes, including the benchmark comparisons, qualitative evaluations in Appendix C.2, and scaling results in Tables 13–14.

M1.justification: The filtering and agentic augmentation pipelines, Qwen3-based model, staged continual pretraining, supervised fine-tuning, and DPO remain unchanged. Appendix D.1 retains the same QLoRA adaptation procedure.

E1.justification: Training corpora and cybersecurity/general evaluation coverage are unchanged. Replacing SECURE's label 'MEAT' with 'MAET' corrects its name to match the existing definition in Appendix C.3; it does not introduce a different task.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 4–6 and 13–14, including the Llama, Qwen, Primus, Foundation-Sec, Lily, DeepHat, and GPT-5 comparisons. No evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Shot counts, metrics, decoding, judging procedures, training budgets, and scaling settings remain unchanged. Appendix B.1 removes the prose statement of a micro-batch size of 32 per GPU, but its configuration retains micro_batch_size: 32 and the stated global batch size remains 1024.

E4.justification: The CyberFineWeb/Seed and post-training comparisons, OpenQA case studies in Figures 12–15, and larger-model scaling analysis in Appendix D.1 are retained. No ablation, robustness test, or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Seed information and statistical reporting are unchanged, including seed 2442 in Appendix B.1 and the score distributions in Figure 6. Neither version adds repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance testing.

E6.justification: Performance entries, rankings, plotted results, and qualitative findings remain unchanged, including Tables 4–6 and 13–14. Table 3 changes '700,1' to '700.1', a decimal-format correction for the same 700,133,360-token total reported in Table 9 in both versions.

T1.justification: There are no changes to mathematical definitions, assumptions, or reasoning. Neither version presents theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about the training resources, agentic augmentation, RedSage-Bench, locally deployable model, and cybersecurity/general benchmark gains.

C2.justification: Interpretations of the training components, tool-use difficulty, and larger-model scalability are unchanged. Sections 5 and 7 retain the same qualifications concerning synthetic-data inaccuracies, misuse, licensing, and research-only deployment.

D1.justification: Section 8 changes datasets, code, and evaluation pipelines from 'will be' to 'are' released, while new acknowledgments identify Leonardo at CINECA as computing support. Configurations and access links remain unchanged. Actual release status remains ambiguous because the abstract already claimed availability and the conclusion still promises release.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 removes the explicit argument that encoder-based predecessors require task-specific fine-tuning that restricts scalability, replacing it with a shorter description of their unreleased datasets as task-specific. The cited works and central novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes limited grammar and terminology corrections, including 'Evaluation-Planer' to 'Evaluation-Planner', shortens several passages, adjusts paragraph placement, and adds acknowledgments. The overall section structure and narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 3 moves above Figure 4, Figure 6 moves from page 9 to page 8 with a shorter caption, and surrounding material is repaginated. The SFT configuration now spans pages 41–42, and Tables 5 and 14 correct the MAET header. The same figures and tables are retained.

improvement.justification: Correcting the SECURE acronym to match Appendix C.3, fixing Table 3's decimal formatting, and editing grammatical errors modestly improve clarity and consistency. Added funding and computing acknowledgments improve transparency. The scientific evidence and conclusions remain unchanged, and conflicting release-status statements persist, limiting the reproducibility benefit.
